| | Dear , **TRAN VS TRAHAN DEBATE** ** ** **Speaking Truth To Power** ** ** ** ** Over one hundred people gathered at Moloney hall Friday to witness the debate between Congresswoman Democrat Lori Trahan and her Republican challenger, former State Senator Dean Tran. The excitement and tension began building early as several Tran and Trahan supporters lined the streets outside the University Crossing building on Pawtucket Street in Lowell. The evenly divided partisan crowd helped to energize a debate that Democrat party insiders wanted to keep low key. Half way through the debate, all inhibitions seemed to be cast aside and both candidates engaged in a vigorous, debate over the pressing problems facing the district and nation at this time. Prominent among these were the economy, election integrity, fentanyl abuse, abortion and freedom. Clear differences became very apparent. Here is rundown on these and other issues: **The Economy:** ** ** Congresswoman Trahan stuck to the straight Democrat party line on the economy alleging that inflation was caused by global conditions, particularly the invasion of Ukraine by Putin’s Russia, and that Biden’s inflation reduction act was a decisive step in addressing it. Senator Tran struck back accusing Trahan of supporting Biden’s spending proposals, which he charged was the direct cause of inflation. Tran quoted Steve Ratner, an Obama economic advisor, who said that the 1.9T infrastructure bill, which was passed by Congress on strict partisan lines, was the single most direct cause of inflation. Tran then took the offensive and accused the “Biden-Pelosi-Trahan” administration of increasing heating prices, describing this problem as “self-inflicted”. He said that many people are going to spend a very cold and expensive winter this year because of Biden’s decision to curb the domestic fossil fuel industry, in particular killing the XL pipeline. Senator Tran ended his remarks by quoting another Obama economic advisor, Larry Summers, who said that “Biden’s mistakes have caused the energy crisis.” ** ** **Abortion: ** ** ** Congresswoman Trahan pledged herself to the defense of a women’s right to choose. She told the audience that if the Republicans retake the House and Senate, they will pass a bill that will limit abortion to only the first 15 weeks of pregnancy and implied that her opponent was a supporter of that legislation. Senator Tran responded by saying that the US Congress should not make any rulings on abortion at all. He said that he would not support any proposed limitation on abortion in the House because in his judgement these are matters that should be left to the states. Trahan fired back saying that she was a firm supporter of the Roe Act, a bill that recently extended the period that a woman could have an abortion, and she accused Senator Tran of being against the act. Tran responded by saying that he would never support the killing of any child who was at the point of birth ** ** **Drugs and Mental Health:** ** ** Congresswoman Trahan acknowledged that drug abuse was a major contributing factor to the mental illness and suicide problem in the nation. She pledged more federal money for mental wellness. Senator Tran pointed to Biden’s failed record on border security, claiming that this was a major factor in contributing to drug abuse and mental illness. He alleged that it was the reason for the high volume of fentanyl laced drugs coming into the country, threatening our children and young adults. He described Congresswoman Trahan’s record on border security as dismal and said that her support for the Biden administration was allowing the chaos on the southern border to continue. She responded by denying that the border was in chaos, and said that illegal entries were being controlled by electronic means and “not by some foolish wall,” to which cries of “build the wall” rose from the audience. ** ****Elections And Free Speech:** ** ** Moderator John Cluverius interjected himself only twice during the debate, allowing a panel of students to do the bulk of the candidate questioning. However, he asked both Senator Tran and Congresswoman Trahan if they would accept the results of the next election. Both answered in the affirmative. Cluverius then went on to ask Senator Tran, if he had to choose between fair elections and unrestricted free speech, which would he choose. This question drew boos and loud catcalls from the audience branding Cluverius’s question as a “false choice”. Senator Tran calmly asked the moderator, if he was asking him to make a choice between fair elections and free speech? Cluverius nodded in the affirmative. Tran said that both conditions were equally important in a democracy and then refused to accept the premise of the question. Tran’s response lead to a heated response from Congresswoman Trahan in which she alleged that the attack on the Capitol on January 6th 2021 by protesters was ‘an attack upon our democracy” and that the “Republicans were a bunch of “climate deniers”. She drew a loud crescendo of boos from the Republicans in the audience. ** ** **The US Supreme Court:** ** ** In a surprising revelation, Congresswoman Trahan said that she would support an expansion of the Supreme Court. She said that the court was out of touch with the American people. Senator Tran branded the Congresswoman as a “SCOTUS Denier” and affirmed his support for a nine member US supreme court. **The Federal Minimum Wage, Social Security and Medicare.** ** ** In response to a question from the student panel on whether he would increase the minimum wage, Senator Tran characterized the question as “hypothetical”. He said that before the minimum wage was increased there must be a study of its impacts because they would not be the same across the nation. While some state economies might benefit, Tran said others might not. Congresswoman Trahan affirmed her full support for increasing the minimum wage and said that is was “up to the Federal government to ensure a living wage for people.” Trahan told the audience that House Republican leader Kevin McCarthy had pledge to cut social security and Medicare if the Republicans win a majority in both the House and Senate. She asked Senator Tran what he would do. He said that he would not cut social security nor Medicare, and he did not care what pledges Kevin McCarthy was making, because he would place the needs of his constituents first. **Constituency Services and Bi-Partisanship:** ** ** The candidates were asked questions about the district and about working across the aisle in Washington in a highly charged political environment. Congresswoman Trahan attacked Senator Tran by saying that despite his criticism over the infrastructure bill, he was constantly calling her on the phone for assistance with the expansion of route 2. Senator Trahan teed off on that question saying that the reason he called so much was because she wasn’t “doing anything”. He said that route 2 expansion and redesign is the most critical economic issue in the third district and described the Congresswoman as nowhere to be found on it. He noted that only a small portion of the Federal infrastructure bill actually went to infrastructure projects. He branded the bill as “pork barrel spending.” On the question of bi-partisanship the Congresswoman said that she meets regularly with Republicans across the aisle to discuss mutual initiatives. Senator Tran quickly pointed out that she was not bipartisan, that she voted 100% of the time with Biden and Pelosi. **Closing** ** ** It was perhaps in the closing where the sharpest differences between both candidates became apparent. Congresswoman Trahan looked a bit relieved that the arduous debate had concluded. She thanked everyone in the audience for coming and said that she wanted to continue to serve the working people of the third district and asked for their vote. Senator Tran told the audience that he was one of the Vietnamese boat people as an infant, who fled communist oppression. He shared that he was raised in one of the toughest refugee camps in the world, waiting for a green card to come to the USA. He said that he remains grateful and thankful for the opportunity to come to the United States and that because of his experiences he understood the conditions and concerns of the district better than the incumbent. He concluded his remarks with a firm and unequivocal resolve saying : “ I don’t want this country to become like the country that I left” to which his supporters rose with thunderous applause. He then asked for everyone’s vote. ** ** ** ** TRAN WORKS LOCAL MEDIA ** ** **Local Cable: A Key Part To Messaging Strategy** ** ** Former State Senator Dean Tran is employing an aggressive strategy to utilize local media to get his message out to voters. He has recently appeared on local cable in Westford’s Second Opinion program, hosted by Kathy Lynch. Senator Tran has also cut a three minute overview of his campaign for you tube. Both of these are attached for your review. ** ** **Senator Tran’s Three Minute Address On The State of The Nation ( 3 minutes)** ** ** [**https://youtu.be/t1kdaDQrWcY**](https://trk.klclick2.com/ls/click?upn=u4dgWLvf-2F9xYmewse6tZcykixez3EWLHo7vJ3pMQ8r-2B0Gk-2FzZXQq78mpPDJz0J5FZSMVA1b7MJ8FTmuDe1wF8xoTjr0C2hJwK5fBCiHFw4uCu5D2rPA1ON6b7P95iDfOJ9d5_XwU9lPq5-2Bze3gI64ohlV0cQwWAuBAU7ADIvj2CS7ymhPNoyNNs9JMNQ4Sbb-2BxTu6RxkjmEI5QdzmbFRn9RJuC5ZScgP6jG2TPT5Ngue2gB3bhtC0Mwz33l9MQL9rJjvC8Oa55lONZw0XwLwIMBaLJOikE3Sis3L8iQeeOtIgBsCYkSLqG4iTrMajd4j7z4-2BiZI-2B125OP4zRwvYg2JYY-2FnSMqRvSq1ZjIFHFMUz6VxFGVMERLlT5wuRR6BBwwZVMvZRBWWNdTGyMWhwQ2G4MaKcp6BQlRueJjd1mHS9Q3jVP04NLFrfbYohXKcNgtemxx7C3bZwWnMfIxmsUtheP03QhSSwYAR5ddrDhg1xK-2FwfLGJBmK-2FT1rWkOnEvulbYL9HALsmGexej9P1ZO9Wsxnth05H-2F8d-2B-2Bjpp-2Fn8iGnFEsw-3D)** _ _** _ _ **Senator Tran Appears on Westford’s Second Opinion (30 minutes)** ** ** [**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K8zzALPPP24**](https://trk.klclick2.com/ls/click?upn=u4dgWLvf-2F9xYmewse6tZc8C966G4BcTeEZBUQn0-2BOxIAsgGM64t04rWb3BrHWHpaE-2B3crXdAF-2FICkP4Y80w9DhiaAogHD6bYBZ12vaRtVSJpWCMwk9lJDYvvQuOeBJtWJNogbwSIL52YaAwPeodMpg-3D-3D8NBJ_XwU9lPq5-2Bze3gI64ohlV0cQwWAuBAU7ADIvj2CS7ymhPNoyNNs9JMNQ4Sbb-2BxTu6RxkjmEI5QdzmbFRn9RJuC5ZScgP6jG2TPT5Ngue2gB3bhtC0Mwz33l9MQL9rJjvC8Oa55lONZw0XwLwIMBaLJOikE3Sis3L8iQeeOtIgBsCYkSLqG4iTrMajd4j7z4-2BiZI-2B125OP4zRwvYg2JYY-2FnSMqRvSq1ZjIFHFMUz6VxFGVMERLlT5wuRR6BBwwZVMvxGvw6o94LUvCqyf9kz3K45-2FUUgM-2FFb2IxGKePxOvTYkHFszmwZIx9jaUnvjsAbRY254iWyAfWV4iItcSAoioHoaVQK1iEkBdbFmhg2ZambxWIuJ8DdjkvSci-2Fwgx-2FeY3V9-2B8s-2BlY6Gp-2FfeWkWEu5hZVfpsv-2BjjTWgUVSkLK76ms-3D)

clean_body: Over a hundred people witnessed a spicy debate that hit hard on issues | | | | | | | | | | Dear , TRAN VS TRAHAN DEBATE Speaking Truth To Power Over one hundred people gathered at Moloney hall Friday to witness the debate between Congresswoman Democrat Lori Trahan and her Republican challenger, former State Senator Dean Tran. The excitement and tension began building early as several Tran and Trahan supporters lined the streets outside the University Crossing building on Pawtucket Street in Lowell. The evenly divided partisan crowd helped to energize a debate that Democrat party insiders wanted to keep low key. Half way through the debate, all inhibitions seemed to be cast aside and both candidates engaged in a vigorous, debate over the pressing problems facing the district and nation at this time. Prominent among these were the economy, election integrity, fentanyl abuse, abortion and freedom. Clear differences became very apparent. Here is rundown on these and other issues: The Economy: Congresswoman Trahan stuck to the straight Democrat party line on the economy alleging that inflation was caused by global conditions, particularly the invasion of Ukraine by Putin’s Russia, and that Biden’s inflation reduction act was a decisive step in addressing it. Senator Tran struck back accusing Trahan of supporting Biden’s spending proposals, which he charged was the direct cause of inflation. Tran quoted Steve Ratner, an Obama economic advisor, who said that the 1.9T infrastructure bill, which was passed by Congress on strict partisan lines, was the single most direct cause of inflation. Tran then took the offensive and accused the “Biden-Pelosi-Trahan” administration of increasing heating prices, describing this problem as “self-inflicted”. He said that many people are going to spend a very cold and expensive winter this year because of Biden’s decision to curb the domestic fossil fuel industry, in particular killing the XL pipeline. Senator Tran ended his remarks by quoting another Obama economic advisor, Larry Summers, who said that “Biden’s mistakes have caused the energy crisis.” Abortion: Congresswoman Trahan pledged herself to the defense of a women’s right to choose. She told the audience that if the Republicans retake the House and Senate, they will pass a bill that will limit abortion to only the first 15 weeks of pregnancy and implied that her opponent was a supporter of that legislation. Senator Tran responded by saying that the US Congress should not make any rulings on abortion at all. He said that he would not support any proposed limitation on abortion in the House because in his judgement these are matters that should be left to the states. Trahan fired back saying that she was a firm supporter of the Roe Act, a bill that recently extended the period that a woman could have an abortion, and she accused Senator Tran of being against the act. Tran responded by saying that he would never support the killing of any child who was at the point of birth Drugs and Mental Health: Congresswoman Trahan acknowledged that drug abuse was a major contributing factor to the mental illness and suicide problem in the nation. She pledged more federal money for mental wellness. Senator Tran pointed to Biden’s failed record on border security, claiming that this was a major factor in contributing to drug abuse and mental illness. He alleged that it was the reason for the high volume of fentanyl laced drugs coming into the country, threatening our children and young adults. He described Congresswoman Trahan’s record on border security as dismal and said that her support for the Biden administration was allowing the chaos on the southern border to continue. She responded by denying that the border was in chaos, and said that illegal entries were being controlled by electronic means and “not by some foolish wall,” to which cries of “build the wall” rose from the audience. Elections And Free Speech: Moderator John Cluverius interjected himself only twice during the debate, allowing a panel of students to do the bulk of the candidate questioning. However, he asked both Senator Tran and Congresswoman Trahan if they would accept the results of the next election. Both answered in the affirmative. Cluverius then went on to ask Senator Tran, if he had to choose between fair elections and unrestricted free speech, which would he choose. This question drew boos and loud catcalls from the audience branding Cluverius’s question as a “false choice”. Senator Tran calmly asked the moderator, if he was asking him to make a choice between fair elections and free speech? Cluverius nodded in the affirmative. Tran said that both conditions were equally important in a democracy and then refused to accept the premise of the question. Tran’s response lead to a heated response from Congresswoman Trahan in which she alleged that the attack on the Capitol on January 6th 2021 by protesters was ‘an attack upon our democracy” and that the “Republicans were a bunch of “climate deniers”. She drew a loud crescendo of boos from the Republicans in the audience. The US Supreme Court: In a surprising revelation, Congresswoman Trahan said that she would support an expansion of the Supreme Court. She said that the court was out of touch with the American people. Senator Tran branded the Congresswoman as a “SCOTUS Denier” and affirmed his support for a nine member US supreme court. The Federal Minimum Wage, Social Security and Medicare. In response to a question from the student panel on whether he would increase the minimum wage, Senator Tran characterized the question as “hypothetical”. He said that before the minimum wage was increased there must be a study of its impacts because they would not be the same across the nation. While some state economies might benefit, Tran said others might not. Congresswoman Trahan affirmed her full support for increasing the minimum wage and said that is was “up to the Federal government to ensure a living wage for people.” Trahan told the audience that House Republican leader Kevin McCarthy had pledge to cut social security and Medicare if the Republicans win a majority in both the House and Senate. She asked Senator Tran what he would do. He said that he would not cut social security nor Medicare, and he did not care what pledges Kevin McCarthy was making, because he would place the needs of his constituents first. Constituency Services and Bi-Partisanship: The candidates were asked questions about the district and about working across the aisle in Washington in a highly charged political environment. Congresswoman Trahan attacked Senator Tran by saying that despite his criticism over the infrastructure bill, he was constantly calling her on the phone for assistance with the expansion of route 2. Senator Trahan teed off on that question saying that the reason he called so much was because she wasn’t “doing anything”. He said that route 2 expansion and redesign is the most critical economic issue in the third district and described the Congresswoman as nowhere to be found on it. He noted that only a small portion of the Federal infrastructure bill actually went to infrastructure projects. He branded the bill as “pork barrel spending.” On the question of bi-partisanship the Congresswoman said that she meets regularly with Republicans across the aisle to discuss mutual initiatives. Senator Tran quickly pointed out that she was not bipartisan, that she voted 100% of the time with Biden and Pelosi. Closing It was perhaps in the closing where the sharpest differences between both candidates became apparent. Congresswoman Trahan looked a bit relieved that the arduous debate had concluded. She thanked everyone in the audience for coming and said that she wanted to continue to serve the working people of the third district and asked for their vote. Senator Tran told the audience that he was one of the Vietnamese boat people as an infant, who fled communist oppression. He shared that he was raised in one of the toughest refugee camps in the world, waiting for a green card to come to the USA. He said that he remains grateful and thankful for the opportunity to come to the United States and that because of his experiences he understood the conditions and concerns of the district better than the incumbent. He concluded his remarks with a firm and unequivocal resolve saying : “ I don’t want this country to become like the country that I left” to which his supporters rose with thunderous applause. He then asked for everyone’s vote. body:
We all need to do our part
#
Peter,
I’ve spent a third of my adult life living out of a suitcase overseas. I’ve spent the rest of it firmly rooted in my hometown of Edmonds, Washington. (I can look out my window right now and see my old junior high school.)
My travels have taught me a lot including three points I’d like to share now: 1) You learn a lot about your own home (and society) by leaving it and looking at it from afar. 2) Fear is for people who don’t get out much. 3) And democracy is fragile. And I’ve come to believe that if everyone could travel before they voted, our economy would be more robust, more fair, and more sustainable, our country would be stronger, and the world would be a better and more stable place.
I’ve seen a lot of great places. But I’d only live in one...and that’s right here. I care deeply about my community, my state, my country, and the world, and strongly believe we all have a part to play to make our society a better and more just place — and so does Patty Murray.
**[I’m proud to have been a big Patty supporter for a long time. She has always been a strong, committed leader for Washington state but she needs all our help to win. Can you contribute $5 now to help make sure we reelect Patty?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/53265180/374932636/1316305760?refcode=pm_em_221024_2&amount=5&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&firstname=Peter&lastname=&addr1=&city=Cresco&state=PA&phone=&employer=&occupation=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YWRkZWMxZC0xMTU0LWVkMTEtODE5Yy0wMDIyNDgyNThlMDgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=G474iALpwLt60CoTQFtd9yA0I4w4boAVeYhUvr3xA8g=)**
Being an effective legislator for a state is more than complaining and promising tax cuts. Legislating is a skill and — people of any political persuasion agree on this: Patty Murray is a brilliant legislator.
I employ a hundred people here in my small town. I’m an enthusiastic capitalist who believes that for capitalism to more than soar — to soar in a way that works for those whose hard work makes it soar — it needs a referee. And that referee is a smart and caring government. I’m a leader in my church and I believe that we should love our neighbor and take care of those who are in need and hungry. I believe a healthy debate between principled conservatives and liberals on issues like these is good for the fabric of our society. I also believe that this election is about more than politics. It will shape how our great country is governed going forward. We need public leaders who are working to bring people together, find solutions, make our communities better and to make our democracy stronger. That’s Patty.
**[There are only a few weeks left in this election. One way you can do your part is by chipping in $5 right now to support Patty Murray in this election.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/53265181/374932637/1316305760?refcode=pm_em_221024_2&amount=5&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&firstname=Peter&lastname=&addr1=&city=Cresco&state=PA&phone=&employer=&occupation=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YWRkZWMxZC0xMTU0LWVkMTEtODE5Yy0wMDIyNDgyNThlMDgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=G474iALpwLt60CoTQFtd9yA0I4w4boAVeYhUvr3xA8g=)**
Thank you,
Rick Steves
American Travel Writer

clean_body: We all need to do our part Peter, I’ve spent a third of my adult life living out of a suitcase overseas. I’ve spent the rest of it firmly rooted in my hometown of Edmonds, Washington. (I can look out my window right now and see my old junior high school.) My travels have taught me a lot including three points I’d like to share now: 1) You learn a lot about your own home (and society) by leaving it and looking at it from afar. 2) Fear is for people who don’t get out much. 3) And democracy is fragile. And I’ve come to believe that if everyone could travel before they voted, our economy would be more robust, more fair, and more sustainable, our country would be stronger, and the world would be a better and more stable place. I’ve seen a lot of great places. But I’d only live in one...and that’s right here. I care deeply about my community, my state, my country, and the world, and strongly believe we all have a part to play to make our society a better and more just place — and so does Patty Murray. = Being an effective legislator for a state is more than complaining and promising tax cuts. Legislating is a skill and — people of any political persuasion agree on this: Patty Murray is a brilliant legislator. I employ a hundred people here in my small town. I’m an enthusiastic capitalist who believes that for capitalism to more than soar — to soar in a way that works for those whose hard work makes it soar — it needs a referee. And that referee is a smart and caring government. I’m a leader in my church and I believe that we should love our neighbor and take care of those who are in need and hungry. I believe a healthy debate between principled conservatives and liberals on issues like these is good for the fabric of our society. I also believe that this election is about more than politics. It will shape how our great country is governed going forward. We need public leaders who are working to bring people together, find solutions, make our communities better and to make our democracy stronger. That’s Patty. = Thank you, Rick Steves American Travel Writer ** ****=**** As Washington's senior U.S. Senator, Patty Murray is working to help families, solve problems, and defend our progressive values._ PAID FOR BY PEOPLE FOR PATTY MURRAY

subject: When they try to doubt you...
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Cheri Beasley for North Carolina
body:
#

Hi there,
As I was drinking my tea this morning, I was reflecting on this race, and it reminded me of something I said shortly after I became Chief Justice. So I wanted to share it with you and how I’m feeling about the final two weeks of this race.
From the start, I knew there would be people who would doubt me and this campaign. It’s a reality we’ve all faced at some point in our lives.
Some might whisper about if North Carolinians are ready to elect their first African American Senator. A year ago, pundits certainly tried to doubt that we could win this Senate seat at all.
But sitting here today, those naysayers who doubted us have been forced to acknowledge that North Carolina is in play. We’ve seen multiple tied polls. They’re calling our race “deadlocked,” and CNN says it is one of the seats most likely to flip on Election Day. That is a testament to what we have collectively accomplished. We’ve tried something different with a truly people-powered campaign, and now it is coming down to the wire.
Overcoming these kinds of questions and doubts reminded me of when I said this shortly after becoming Chief Justice: **_“There are times when people tell you that you can’t do something, and really it has to do more with the confinement of their own ability to see it.”**_
I am really excited to run as hard as we can in these final days. We’ve got Republicans panicked. We are giving them the fight of their life, and a historic victory is absolutely within reach. But it’s our job to make sure we don’t slow down or falter for even a moment, so I need to ask you today:
[**Will you please make a $3 donation to our campaign to flip North Carolina? This is our best chance to expand the majority and change what people think is possible in the U.S. Senate.**](https://act.cheribeasley.com/go/2567?c0=cb-em-oct22.I3buyh&refcode=em221024-2-T1&t=1&akid=2112%2E357359%2Ed0BNPm)

April 26, 2021

Do you remember, folks? That’s the day we launched this
whirlwind campaign for Ohio’s open Senate seat.

Together, we’ve built an incredible movement—meeting with folks in all of
Ohio’s 88 counties, securing the Democratic nomination for Senate, and
countering the far right’s BS lies. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished
so far and hopeful for the fight ahead.

350,000

That’s the number of folks who have chipped in their hard-earned dollars
to this campaign. Without your donations, we wouldn’t stand a chance
against JD Vance’s billionaire backers and the GOP’s dark money machine.

This is exactly the kind of grassroots power it will take to win this
neck-and-neck race, and I couldn’t be more grateful to have you in my
corner.

$10

That’s the amount I’m asking you to chip in today—because it’s not about
how much you give, but how many people we have on the team.

There’s power in numbers, and I’ll take thousands of
hardworking folks chipping in what they can, when they can, over a blank
check from some corporate billionaire any day.

[ https://act.timforoh.com/go/28341?t=1009&amount=10&akid=6248%2E3611125%2ETowZnR ]So, I’m humbly asking: will you please make a $10 contribution to our
campaign right now? We're in the final stretch of this race and we can’t

Fellow Patriot,

I have always believed every American deserves justice...

But I never knew we'd have to fight so hard to get it.

My husband is Chief Petty Officer Eric Gilmet of the United States Navy and right now a corrupt system is threatening to rip him away from our family for decades. HELP OUR FAMILY SEEK JUSTICE >> (https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av)
https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av

Eric is charged alongside fellow servicemen Gunnery Sergeant Danny Draher and Gunnery Sergeant Josh Negron who were all deployed to Iraq to fight for our country. They call them the “MARSOC 3.”

Let me tell you the full story...

It all started at a bar when a civilian contractor, who had been fighting with other customers, began fighting with my husband, Draher, and Negron. The contractor was escorted from the bar, and all was well until the MARSOC 3 decided to go home for the evening.

Upon leaving the bar, they were confronted by the contractor, and a fight ensued that knocked the contractor to the ground. My husband stayed with the man for hours, even bringing him back to base for medical care throughout the night.

But, the contractor tragically passed due to complications from his intoxicated state - and my nightmare began.
https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av

Our trial was one miscarriage of justice after the other. Our defense team was threatened. Our case was completely compromised. So much so that it was actually dismissed with prejudice on February 9th...

That was a huge relief, but that ruling has been overturned. They’ve ruled that “any conflict of interest was purely subjective.”

I’m telling you, it was not subjective and this is NOT justice. FIGHT FOR JUSTICE >> (https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av)

There is overwhelming evidence that the MARSOC 3 acted in self-defense/defense of others. But still, my husband and the Marine Raiders could face prison time for involuntary manslaughter, negligent homicide, obstructing justice, and violations of orders.

United American Patriots (UAP) has supported all of our families during our lengthy legal battle by funding our civilian legal representation and continuously generating awareness to members of Congress and to the public about the facts of the case.

Now, as we move forward toward overcoming this new obstacle, they're helping us again to find justice in an overwhelmingly corrupt system.

But today, I'm asking for your help, too. Will you fight for the MARSOC 3 today by donating United American Patriots?
https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av
FREE THE 3: $100 (https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av)
FREE THE 3: $75 (https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av)
FREE THE 3: $50 (https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av)
FREE THE 3: $25 (https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av)

The truth is that families like mine would be overwhelmed with these battles if not for UAP.

United American Patriots works with families like mine to find an effective legal defense team and alleviate the financial burden of these long, drawn-out trials.

They make sure we have the best attorneys, investigators, and experts on their side to preserve our rights and defend against wrongful accusations and convictions.

If you can donate to UAP today, your gift would be a godsend to my husband’s legal defense that could very well help him avoid prison - and stay with our family, where we need him.

That would mean the world to me.
URGENT DONATION: $35 (https://secure.winred.com/united-american-patriots-inc/action-av-7158157/?utm_source=av&utm_medium=7158157&utm_campaign=prosp&utm_term=mindy_gilmet&utm_content=av)

Thank you for reading our story, and I appreciate anything you can give.

Mindy Gilmet

Team,
The Washington Post recently joined Elissa for a full day on the campaign trail. Their article was just published, and it represents the larger story of the election coming in just 15 days.
https://wapo.st/3VYGx3O [https://wapo.st/3VYGx3O]
The majority of the day was spent in Shiawassee county. It’s a conservative area – Dems tend to get about 35% percent of the vote — but showing up in areas that don’t typically lean Democratic has always been part of Elissa’s strategy. The only way she wins in Trump-voting areas is by “losing better” in these areas – which means showing up again and again in places that havent seen a Democrat show up in years. We’re talking to folks about the economy, bringing our supply chains back home, and lowering the cost of prescription drugs.
One of the main things Elissa imparted to the Washington Post AND to folks on the campaign trail: are we going to use the tough times we’re going through as a nation as a political talking point? Or are we actually going to do something about it? Real leaders lead with hope and purpose, they don’t draw happiness from the pain of their residents.
We hope you check out the full article. And if you’re interested in helping Elissa continue to tackle our toughest challenges head on, consider making a contribution below. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/slotkinq42022?refcode=email20221024_2&amount=28]

body:
[1]Charles Booker

Hi, it’s Charles Booker, the Democratic nominee running for U.S. Senate in
Kentucky against Rand Paul.

If my heartless opponent had it his way, the federal government would cut
every social service, including Medicare, Social Security, food benefits
for children, and more.

He’d pass a big-government, restrictive anti-abortion law to restrict
women’s reproductive rights at the local, state, and federal levels.

He’d do everything in his power to waste Kentucky’s time and attention on
issues that won’t improve our lives.

[ https://act.charlesbooker.org/go/18789?t=1001&akid=2656%2E346206%2EHcUmoP ]This is what’s on the line. This is why we must win. So I need to ask

help me DEFEAT Rand Paul in November?

My name is Charles Booker. I’m on a mission to defeat Rand Paul and
restore leadership to the Senate and representation for Kentucky, from the
Hood to the Holler.

Thanks,

Charles Booker
